text: answer[mkt-1789265111792-f8993a]: Dallas, November 22, 1963. Three shots shattered the afternoon—and the story America told itself. The Warren Commission concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald, acting alone, killed President John F. Kennedy from the sixth floor of the Texas School Book Depository. But a nation in shock heard echoes in every shadow: a second gunman, a hidden plot, intelligence agencies, organized crime, Cuba, the Soviet Union. Decades later, the evidence remains disputed, the records incomplete, and the question refuses to die. So who actually killed JFK? The most defensible answer is still Oswald—but “defensible” is not the same as satisfying. Tonight, we separate what is documented from what is merely suspected, examine the witnesses and ballistic evidence, and ask why this murder became America’s enduring crime scene.
